# Box Specification

A box specification describes a machine in your own cloud as a TOML file: its CPUs, memory, disk, system and region, the `lnk` installed on it, what it attaches, and how a box made here is isolated. The `box` specification is TOML, given to a command that reads it as a file, and a field flag sets the field it names, overriding the file. Its JSON Schema is [`box.schema.json`](box.schema.json).

## Use It

Give `lnk box check`, `lnk box create`, and `lnk box size list` a `box` specification as a file, and set any field below with its field flag, which overrides the file. `lnk box spec show` prints the specification as it is read.

## Every Option

Every field the reader takes, with an example value.

```toml
kind = "box"
schema = 1
deadline = "4h"
env = "env.toml"
link_tags = ["lnk-group=example"]
name = "web"
self_remove = true
version = 3

[attach]
address = "fixed"
disks = ["data"]
identity = "service"
network = "control"

[isolation]
no_sandbox = false
sandbox = "box-sandbox.toml"

[lnk]
login = true
version = "1.0.0"

[machine]
arch = "x86_64"
os = "ubuntu-24.04"
spot = true

[machine.aws]
region = "eu-west-2"
size = "g6.xlarge"
spot = false

[machine.aws.disk]
min = "80 GB"

[machine.aws.tags]
cost = "ci"

[machine.cpus]
max = 4
min = 2

[machine.disk]
min = "40 GB"
type = "fast"

[machine.gcp]
os = "ubuntu-22.04"
region = "europe-west2"

[machine.gcp.memory]
max = "32 GB"
min = "8 GB"

[machine.gpus]
max = 2
min = 1
model = "nvidia-l4"

[machine.memory]
max = "16 GB"
min = "4 GB"

[machine.tags]
project = "research"
```

## `attach`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--attach`

Existing resources attached to the machine, which the box uses and never creates or deletes.

### `address`

> **Type** text · **Flag** `--attach.address`

A reserved address it takes: the address's name on Google Cloud; on AWS, its allocation ID. Kept when the box is deleted.

### `disks`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Flag** `--attach.disks`

Data disks it attaches, never formats and keeps when it's deleted: persistent disks' names on Google Cloud; on AWS, volumes' IDs, each in its subnet's availability zone.

### `identity`

> **Type** text · **Flag** `--attach.identity`

Who it acts as in its cloud: a service account's name or email on Google Cloud; on AWS, an instance profile's name.

### `network`

> **Type** text · **Flag** `--attach.network`

The network it joins: a network's name on Google Cloud; on AWS, a subnet's ID whose VPC has an `lnk-box` security group.

## `deadline`

> **Type** text · **Flag** `--deadline`

How long the box lives, from one second through seven days, such
as `30m`, `4h` or `7d`. Left out, it lives until it's deleted.

## `env`

> **Type** text · **Flag** `--env`

The environment file the box is set up from, at every placement,
captured once when the box is made and started again at each `lnk
box start`. Left out, the box has no application setup.

## `isolation`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--isolation`

How a box made here is isolated: in its sandbox, the default, or directly. A box in a cloud account is a machine of its own, so it refuses the whole table.

### `no_sandbox`

> **Type** `true` or `false` · **Flag** `--isolation.no_sandbox`

Whether it runs directly, with your own access and no sandbox;
refused where this machine's policy says `unsandboxed = false`.

### `sandbox`

> **Type** text · **Flag** `--isolation.sandbox`

The sandbox specification it runs in; given with no file, it only runs in
its sandbox again.

### `vm`

> **Type** text · **Unavailable** this build of Link has no VM provider · **Flag** `--isolation.vm`

A VM specification, for a workload in a VM, relative to its file. This
build has no VM provider, so a file naming one is refused, never
run in a sandbox instead.

## `link_tags`

> **Type** a list, each text · **Flag** `--link_tags`

Link's own tags on the machine, beside yours, such as the group a
job's boxes are in. Link writes these for its own boxes.

## `lnk`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--lnk`

The `lnk` installed on the box.

### `login`

> **Type** `true` or `false` · **Flag** `--lnk.login`

Whether the box's `lnk` signs in to your Link account, which a box
made for a service turns off with `false`.

### `version`

> **Type** text · **Flag** `--lnk.version`

The `lnk` release to install with its modules, such as `0.14.0` or
a prerelease, 0.11.0 or later. From a file it can't be behind this
computer's `lnk`, so a specification someone hands you can't install a
release with a known hole; `--lnk.version` given yourself can.
Left out, the latest.

## `machine`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--machine`

The machine, as you'd describe one at a store: every cloud gets the
smallest that fits, and a cloud's own table, `[machine.<cloud>]`,
replaces any of its keys on that cloud.

### `arch`

> **Type** one of `x86_64`, `arm64` · **Flag** `--machine.arch`

The processor, `x86_64` by default.

### `cpus`

> **Type** a whole number from 0, or a table · **Flag** `--machine.cpus`

How many CPUs: a count, `4`, or a range, `{ min = 2, max = 8 }`. Left out, the default size's.

#### `max`

> **Type** a whole number from 0 · **Flag** `--machine.cpus.max`

At most this many

#### `min`

> **Type** a whole number from 0 · **Flag** `--machine.cpus.min`

At least this many

### `disk`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--machine.disk`

The boot disk: how big, and how fast. Left out, 20 GB, `balanced`.

#### `min`

> **Type** text · **Flag** `--machine.disk.min`

Its least size, such as `"40 GB"`: what the box gets unless its
image needs more, as NVIDIA's images for a box with GPUs do. 20 GB
by default.

#### `type`

> **Type** one of `balanced`, `fast` · **Flag** `--machine.disk.type`

How fast: `balanced` (gp3 on AWS, pd-balanced on Google Cloud), the default, or `fast` (io2 at 50 IOPS a GB, or pd-ssd), billed for its speed too.

### `gpus`

> **Type** a whole number from 0, or a table · **Flag** `--machine.gpus`

How many GPUs, and which model. Left out, none.

#### `max`

> **Type** a whole number from 0 · **Flag** `--machine.gpus.max`

At most this many

#### `min`

> **Type** a whole number from 0 · **Flag** `--machine.gpus.min`

At least this many

#### `model`

> **Type** one of `nvidia-t4`, `nvidia-l4`, `nvidia-l40s`, `nvidia-a10g`, `nvidia-a100`, `nvidia-h100`, `nvidia-h200`, `nvidia-b200` · **Flag** `--machine.gpus.model`

Which GPU: a model alone means at least one

### `memory`

> **Type** text, or a table · **Flag** `--machine.memory`

How much memory: a size with its unit, `"8 GB"`, or a range of them, `{ min = "4 GB", max = "16 GB" }`. Left out, the default size's.

#### `max`

> **Type** text · **Flag** `--machine.memory.max`

At most this much

#### `min`

> **Type** text · **Flag** `--machine.memory.min`

At least this much

### `os`

> **Type** one of `ubuntu-24.04`, `ubuntu-22.04`, `debian-13`, `macos` · **Flag** `--machine.os`

The system, `ubuntu-24.04` by default.

### `region`

> **Type** text · **Flag** `--machine.region`

Where the box is made: a cloud's region, or on Google Cloud a zone
in it, in a cloud's own table only. `--zone` with `--cloud` sets
the named cloud's. Left out, the account's.

### `size`

> **Type** text · **Flag** `--machine.size`

A machine type, such as `t3.large`, in a cloud's own table only, in
place of `cpus`, `memory` and `gpus`, which it has built in. Left
out, the smallest that fits is picked.

### `spot`

> **Type** `true` or `false` · **Flag** `--machine.spot`

Whether it's a spot machine: cheaper, but the cloud may stop it and
start it again. `false` by default.

### `tags`

> **Type** a table by name, each text · **Flag** `--machine.tags`

Your tags on the machine and its disk, at most 40, each key
starting with a lowercase letter, keys and values lowercase
letters, digits and dashes. Keys starting `lnk-` or `aws:`, and
`Name`, are Link's or the cloud's, and refused.

#### `<name>`

> **Type** text · **Flag** `--machine.tags.<name>`

### `<name>`

> **Type** a table · **Flag** `--machine.<name>`

`[machine]`: its fields, and each cloud's own table, `[machine.<cloud>]`, by the cloud's kind (`aws`, as `lnk cloud list` says): every key of `[machine]`, replacing it on that cloud, and the only place for region and size

## `name`

> **Type** text · **Flag** `--spec.name`

What its boxes are named after: `web` makes `web-1`, `web-2` and so
on. Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter,
at most 27. Left out, the account's name; `--name` still names one
box exactly.

## `self_remove`

> **Type** `true` or `false` · **Flag** `--self_remove`

Whether the machine may remove itself when its work ends, as a box
a job made does.

## `version`

> **Type** a whole number from 0 · **Flag** `--spec.version`

A whole number, yours to bump, which each box remembers it was made
from.
